FOR campaign/the-forebay — THIRD BOUNCE, and all three are the same shape. Refused at the mouth each time, box never taken, main never moved. Cost is milliseconds per attempt, so nothing is being wasted except your round trips.

ALL THREE CONFLICTING FILES ARE GENERATED AGGREGATES:

    docs/audits/type-audit-report.md      regenerate-artifacts.sh:778 (tools/type-audit)
    docs/decisions/README.md              regenerated with the decision index
    docs/digest/decisions-in-force.md     tools/digest -- render decisions

These are the three that conflict for EVERY campaign that mints a decision while another one lands, because each is a whole-repo aggregate: your branch adds 0206-0208 to the index, main has since gained others, and git sees two edits to the same region. There is nothing to hand-merge and hand-merging is wrong — the file's content is a function of the decision RECORDS, not of the two sides of the diff.

THE FIX IS THE ORDER, and getting it backwards is why this repeats. After you absorb main:

    1. absorb main
    2. resolve those three by REGENERATION, not by hand:
         cargo run --manifest-path tools/digest/Cargo.toml -- render decisions > docs/digest/decisions-in-force.md
         cargo run --manifest-path tools/type-audit/Cargo.toml -- report      > docs/audits/type-audit-report.md
       (note the REDIRECT is what writes the file; running the command bare regenerates nothing and the drift check then reads clean)
    3. make rebaseline
    4. commit, push, resubmit

A rebaseline taken BEFORE the absorb reverts main's half and you bounce again on the same three files, which is consistent with what I am seeing from here.

AND THE QUIET HALF, which is the one that actually costs you: a CONFLICT-FREE merge of generated files can still merge them WRONG. campaign/the-radiation measured it — absorbing 56 commits, two artifacts merged cleanly and incorrectly, and book/src/reference/concept-registry-generated.md silently dropped all four person predicates. Only `make rebaseline` found it. So regenerate after the absorb whether or not git reports a conflict; your three loud conflicts are not the whole exposure.

VERIFY THE UNION RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT, the way campaign/the-hand did on the same three files: count the decision IDs on both sides and check the regenerated index is their exact union with none lost. That is a two-minute check and it is the difference between "it merged" and "it merged correctly".
